item.research_question: How does the molten salt corrosion behavior of the dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy compare to conventional duplex stainless steel 2205 in a NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 environment at high temperatures, and what are the underlying mechanisms?
item.material_system: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) and duplex stainless steel 2205 (DS2205)
item.processing_route: Vacuum-arc-melting of high purity constituent elements (99.95 wt.% purity) with multiple re-melting for homogeneity; samples polished to 1200-grit; molten salt prepared by annealing MgCl2, NaCl, and KCl (45.4, 33, 21.6 wt.% respectively) at 300 °C for 24 h in Ar atmosphere
item.test_conditions: Immersion in molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 salt at 450 °C and 650 °C for 24 hours; electrochemical measurements (OCP and potentiodynamic polarization) performed in open air
key_findings: Corrosion rate of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 was ~1 mm/year at 450 °C compared to ~8 mm/year for DS2205.
Corrosion rate of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 was ~9 mm/year at 650 °C compared to ~20 mm/year for DS2205.
Mass loss for DS2205 at 650 °C was ~69 mg/cm² after 24 h, while AlCoCrFeNi2.1 was ~38 mg/cm².
Selective dissolution of the BCC phase (B2 in EHEA, α-Ferrite in DS2205) was observed in both alloys.
Cr depletion depth in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 at 650 °C was ~50 μm, significantly lower than ~300 μm for DS2205.
Volta potential difference between phases was ~50 mV for AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and ~35 mV for DS2205.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 showed enrichment of Co and Ni in the near-surface region due to reduction of impurity ions.
item.mechanism: The superior corrosion resistance of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is attributed to the sacrificial role of Al which forms a redox couple (Al/AlCl3) that reduces the dissolution rate of Cr, Fe, and Ni, and the enrichment of noble elements (Co, Ni) in the protective surface layer. Micro-galvanic coupling between the phases drives selective dissolution of the less noble BCC phase, but the higher volume fraction of the nobler FCC phase and the thermodynamic stability of AlCl3 mitigate overall degradation compared to DS2205.
item.limitations: A detailed evaluation of the effect of moisture content on corrosion behavior has not been performed in the current study.
item.future_work: The effect of moisture content on corrosion behavior is part of a future study.
quotes: The EHEA showed a significantly lower corrosion rate of ~1 mm/year at 450 °C compared to ~8 mm/year for DS2205.
This was attributed to micro-galvanic coupling between the two phases in each alloy that was measured in terms of Volta potential difference using a scanning kelvin probe.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 showed a significantly lower corrosion rate compared to DS2205 at both the temperatures.
